why: B: every compact abstract connected Riemannian ℝⁿ-manifold with any Levi-Civita connection and positive definite (blind) Ricci tensor has, for ALL p, q, Ω(M;p,q) (blind Om, d-topology) homotopy equivalent to a Mathlib CWComplex with finitely many cells in each dimension. A (universes 0; the def pathSpHomotopyEquiv read as Nonempty of its type): for slice submanifolds N ⊆ V with dim ≥ 2, compact, Ricci positive definite, all p, q ∈ N: Ω(N;p,q) has the project's countable cell complex type (cell tower + mapping telescope) with finitely many cells per dimension, and finite-dimensional homology over any field; plus three auxiliary results (a non-conjugate q' joined to q, Ω(N;p,q) ≃ₕ Ω(N;p,q') along a path, homotopy invariance of the cell type). A ⇒ B fails genuinely: abstract manifolds, and the CW-model gap (project tower with non-cellular attaching maps vs Mathlib CWComplex: cellular approximation and CW structure of telescopes missing). B ⇒ A fails genuinely: setting; a Mathlib CW complex does not give the project's tower; homology finiteness would need cellular homology; the auxiliary results are not in B.
